description: Appointed Minister of the Interior, succeeding Bruno Retailleau. Retained the post in the 26 February 2026 reshuffle. Stated priorities: fight against drug trafficking and everyday security.
Headed the Paris police prefecture, succeeding Didier Lallement; oversaw security including the 2024 Paris Olympic Games. Succeeded by Patrice Faure.

role: National Coordinator for Intelligence and Counter-Terrorism (head of CNRLT)
organization: Coordination nationale du renseignement et de la lutte contre le terrorisme (Élysée)
description: Headed the Élysée intelligence and counter-terrorism coordination body, succeeding Pierre de Bousquet de Florian.

role: Secretary of State to the Minister of the Interior
description: Junior minister under Interior Minister Christophe Castaner, responsible notably for coordination of intelligence services and police. Position established for him and abolished after his departure.

organization: Direction générale de la sécurité intérieure
description: Appointed head of the DGSI by President Emmanuel Macron, succeeding Patrick Calvar; pursued a policy of 'openness'. Succeeded by Nicolas Lerner.
Police prefect for the Bouches-du-Rhône department, based in Marseille.

role: Chief of staff (directeur de cabinet), Paris Police Prefecture
description: Directeur de cabinet at the Paris police prefecture.

role: Subprefect of the arrondissement of Bayonne
Chief of staff (directeur de cabinet) to the prefect of Seine-Saint-Denis
description: Directeur de cabinet of the prefect of Seine-Saint-Denis.

role: Senior civil servant (early prefectoral and administrative posts)
description: Entered the French civil service in 1989; graduated from the École nationale d'administration in 1999 and held a series of administrative and prefectoral posts.
